jobs.title: Quality and Food Safety Intern at Flowers Foods
jobs.description: Employer: Flowers Foods Expires: 10/11/2026 Quality and Food Safety InternBringing Home the Dough$20 - $25 an hour— based on projected academic level at time of internship Location: Onsite—Montgomery, AL (does not come with housing) Rising to the Challenge: Position Responsibilities As a Quality and Food Safety Intern, you will support the Quality and Food Safety Manager through practicing the basic principles of food safety and quality assurance. jobs.title: Hayley Petit Prevention Fellowship at Connecticut Children's Medical Center
jobs.description: Employer: Connecticut Children's Medical Center Expires: 10/12/2026 The Hayley Petit Injury and Violence Prevention FellowshipABOUT THE FELLOWSHIP: The Fellowship is an exciting 8-week program with Connecticut Children's Injury Prevention Center (IPC). Selected applicants will participate in this immersion into the field of injury prevention through readings, discussions, and presentations by IPC faculty and staff. Additionally, Fellows may have the opportunity to participate in clinical and community injury prevention job shadows, as well as community outreach events.Fellowship recipients are selected for their interest in injury and violence prevention and public health as expressed in a one page essay (see details below) and indicated by your resume. Each Fellow is awarded a $1000 stipend at the end of the session. Fellows are expected to commit 6 hours a week to the Fellowship, including a weekly in person and remote meeting. In person meetings will be held on Wednesdays 1pm-4pm, at 10 Columbus Boulevard, in Hartford CT. The day and time of the remote meeting will be determined after Fellows are selected. Eligibility: The fellowship is open to students who identify as women, are able to receive federally taxed wages and are currently enrolled in an undergraduate degree-granting program of a college or university. Students should have access to reliable transportation to and from Hartford.Applications Due: October 9, 2026Applicants Notified of Decision: Monday October 19, 2026Program Begins: Wednesday October 21, 2026Program Concludes the week of December 16th, 2026HOW TO APPLY: A complete applicant package includes: Your résumé AND a one page, single space essay (or letter) that explains a) Your interest in injury and violence prevention b) What you hope to accomplish during the fellowship c) How the fellowship connects with your long term career goals.Completed submissions should be emailed to Rebecca Beebe, PhD at rbeebe01@connecticutchildrens.org.

jobs.title: Golf Internship @ Bandon Dunes Golf Resort at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort
jobs.description: Employer: Bandon Dunes Golf Resort Expires: 10/14/2026 As a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, you'll get real hands-on experience at one of the world's top golf destinations while pursuing your Professional Golf Management degree. You'll work directly with guests, manage our golf shop, coordinate tournaments, and learn the business side of golf operations. This isn't just shadowing someone—you'll have actual responsibilities that matter to our guests' experiences on courses that rank among the top 16 public courses in America.About Bandon Dunes Golf Resort:Bandon Dunes is a world-class golf resort located on the Oregon Coast near the charming community of Bandon. Guests come to experience golf as it was meant to be at Bandon Dunes' six distinct golf courses. That includes five 18-hole courses, which all rank among the top 16 public courses in the United States, according to Golf Digest. The resort is also home to an award-winning par-3 course, Bandon Preserve. A second par-3 course, Shorty's, will open in 2024. The two short courses are 'Courses with a Mission,' with all net proceeds funding the Bandon Dunes Charitable Foundation. The Foundation supports communities along the South Coast of Oregon.Beyond premier golf, guests delight in a variety of dining options at Bandon Dunes’ collection of restaurants. Whether you're looking to enjoy locally-sourced, Pacific-Northwest cuisine accompanied by an award-winning wine list, or prefer kicking back in a Scottish-style setting with traditional pub fare and local microbrews, there is something for everyone.Working at Bandon Dunes is a dream for golf fans, outdoor enthusiasts, and hospitality professionals alike. The Bandon Dunes team works together to create trips of a lifetime for our guests. We are passionate stewards of our resort, our community, and our environment. As an endlessly curious group, we ask questions, share ideas, and always look for a better way. With a hard-working attitude, we help guide our guests through their pure golf experience, immersed in Oregon’s natural beauty and away from the demands of daily life.What You'll Do:Learn the retail side of golf. You'll become an expert on our golf shop merchandise, help guests find what they need, and handle special orders. This means understanding products well enough to make real recommendations, not just ringing up sales.Handle real transactions. You'll process merchandise sales, greens fees, and equipment rentals while keeping accurate records. You'll learn the financial side of golf operations through actual daily work, not textbook theory.Provide genuine customer service. You'll answer guest questions, schedule tee times, and maintain professional phone interactions. When guests call, you'll be the voice they hear representing Bandon Dunes.Support tournaments and events. You'll help organize competitions and special events, coordinating between different departments to make sure everything runs smoothly. This is where you'll see how all the moving pieces fit together.Manage inventory and operations. You'll help keep merchandise displays organized, assist with inventory counts, and support various services like handicapping systems and driving range operations.What Makes You a Great Fit:You're pursuing a Professional Golf Management degree. We work with certified PGM programs and prefer students who can commit to a 6-month internship. This gives you enough time to really learn the business, not just get a quick overview.You communicate well. Strong written and verbal skills matter here because you'll interact with guests from around the world. You need to sound professional on the phone and explain complex golf services clearly.You can handle multiple priorities. Golf operations move fast, and you'll need to manage several tasks while staying calm under pressure. If you get flustered easily when things get busy, this probably isn't the right fit.You're flexible with your schedule. Golf doesn't stop for weekends or holidays. You'll work evenings, weekends, and busy periods when our guests need us most.Special Intern Benefits:Shared staff housing available for a reasonable fee, mentorship from industry professionals, and the chance to play golf for free on seven award-winning courses.If you're serious about a career in golf and want to learn the business at one of the world's premier destinations, we'd like to hear from you. This internship will give you real experience you can't get in a classroom, plus the chance to build relationships with industry professionals. You'll work hard, but you'll also get to play some of the best golf of your life on your days off.Ready to embark on an enriching journey in the world of golf? Apply today to become a Golf Intern at Bandon Dunes Golf Resort and be part of a team dedicated to providing one of the world’s most exceptional golfing experiences.At Bandon Dunes Golf Resort, we are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Winter Trail Members at American Conservation Experience
jobs.description: Employer: American Conservation Experience Expires: 10/23/2026 Winter Trail Members - Saguaro National ParkAmerican Conservation Experience, a nonprofit Conservation Corps, in partnership with Saguaro National Park, is seeking 2 Members to contribute to primarily backcountry trail maintenance projects alongside NPS Staff.For more information about ACE, please visit our website.Start Date: 11/2/2026Estimated End Date: 3/13/2027*a 19-week minimum commitment is required * Location Details/Description:Saguaro National Park, Tucson, AZThe Maintenance Headquarters are on the East side of the park, Rincon Mountain District (3693 S Old Spanish Trail) but there is potential to work on the West Side (Tucson Mountain District) of the park depending on the work projects.Saguaro National Park is located outside of the city of Tucson, AZ. The park is host to camping, hiking, and backpacking trails for every level of adventurer. The park protects its namesake, our nation's largest species of cacti, the giant saguaro. Summers in the Sonoran Desert can be extremely hot with temperatures exceeding 110 degrees and evening lows averaging 72 degrees. Winters present comfortable daytime temperatures in the 60s but cooler nighttime temps that often drop below freezing. Access to all major amenities can be found in the town of Tucson which is a quick 20-minute drive from the park.For more information about Saguaro National Park, please visit the NPS website. Position Overview: The ACE Member will serve their season working on trails either in the high country or front country of the desert southwest. Most of this position will consist of backcountry service. The service requires very strenuous effort in moving heavy materials to and around the job site. The Member must be able to hike steep trails in all weather conditions transporting tools and personal gear and work in difficult terrain. Members routinely move items over 50 pounds.The ACE Member will assist with rehabilitating and maintaining the following trail related structures: log cribbing and steps, water bars and culverts, stone retaining walls, and stone steps and other tread structures. Tread improvement, out sloping, berm busting and rock removal will be common. Team members will likely assist in cutting and shaping stone. Tools will include a wide variety of hand and power tools such as various hammers, shovels, stone tools, rock bars, digging tools, and power shop tools such as cut-off saws, grinders, and drill presses. May use powered tracked material haulers. Consistently moves heavy materials to and around the job site. Serves under the supervision of a Trail Work Leader or higher graded trail employee.There are a variety of trail maintenance projects in the Cactus Forest of the Rincon Mountain District, brushing, installing timber check steps, and re-naturalizing parts of the trail. Other potential project work is helping with mine closures, bench installation projects and trail maintenance throughout the park. These projects have the same requirements of hiking, hauling heavy things and trail maintenance tasks.There may also be project work at other southern Arizona Park units such as Organ Pipe National Monument, Tumacácori Historical Park, and others.This individual placement is meant to facilitate professional development and promotes exposure to land management agencies and networking with professionals. This could include gaining experience in different conservation fields and shadowing different work groups.Schedule: Most of this position will consist of backcountry service. When on front country assignments the schedule will run Monday to Thursday with 4 days on, and 3 days off. For backcountry assignments the schedule will run from Wednesday to Wednesday and consist of 8-day hitches, and 6 days off, where team members will be camping in a backcountry or front country setting. Position BenefitsLiving Allowance: The ACE Member is expected to contribute ~40 hours/week and will receive a living allowance of $800/week to offset the costs of food and incidental expenses, dispersed bi-weekly.This position is part of the Public Land Corps Hiring Authority: Members serving under this agreement must meet the PLC Eligibility Requirements to be considered for this position. Members may be eligible for a federal hiring authority upon completion of their term of service and 640 hours of service. If the duration of a PLC-eligible term is not long enough for Members to accrue 640 hours of service (~16 weeks), the total hours served at the completion of the term may be eligible to be combined with hours accrued from another PLC-eligible term to meet the 640 hours requirement. PLC projects also include specific eligibility requirements such as age (You must be between the ages of 16 and 30. Some agencies also interpret these guidelines to include veterans up to age 35) and citizenship. Please contact ACE staff with questions about eligibility, or view general eligibility information on our website.Housing: Housing is the responsibility of the member and not provided by ACE or NPS.Boot Gear Allowance: ACE members will have up to $200 to spend on work boots. Eligible gear must be approved by ACE staff prior to purchase. Provided Training/Orientation: ACE members will receive position specific training and an orientation outlining ACE policies and procedures, clear guidance on prohibited activities, and networks for support. Qualifications Required:Members must be authorized to work in the United States. ACE does not provide sponsorship for employment visas. Willing and able to represent ACE and the partner organization in a professional, positive, and enthusiastic manner. Ability to be both self-directed/work alone, and be a positive, contributing member of a group.A valid driver's license and an insurable driving record (documentation to be provided upon request). Members must be 21+ to drive due to ACE’s insurance and liability requirements.Willing to undergo and must pass the required criminal history checks Ability to perform the essential duties of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.ACE Members will need to complete bi-weekly timesheets, beginning of term feedback forms, end of term evaluations and for longer terms, a mid-term evaluation. Members may not participate in any prohibited activities as listed in the Member Service Agreement.To learn more about eligibility requirements, please visit our website located on our Indeed homepage.Preferred:Competitive applicants for this position can hold or be pursuing an associates or bachelors degree and/or have relevant experience in environmental science, botany, ecosystem restoration, natural resource management, or related discipline.Knowledge of trails maintenance and construction methods.Ability and willingness to hike 15 miles in a variety of potentially harsh environmental conditions and camp in a backcountry or front country setting.Ability and willingness to use a variety of hand tools, carry and move things weighing 50 lbs or moreDeep interest in outdoor recreational pursuits and being a productive part of a team. Physical Demands, Work Environment and Working Conditions: Physical Demands: Requires frequent sitting, standing, walking, hiking, carrying, using hands to handle or feel, reaching with hands and arms, talking and hearing. Manual dexterity required for use of various tools.. Required to stoop, kneel, climb stairs, and/or crouch. Ability to hike over rough terrain, and camp overnight under field conditions.Vision Requirements: Requires close, distance, peripheral and depth perception vision as well as the ability to focus.Weight Lifted or Force Exerted: Frequently moves up to 50 lbs., ability to move up to 50 pounds.Environmental: Outdoor conditions. Work environment conditions can change frequently; working under adverse weather conditions and in various climates Noise Environment: Moderate to high noise such gas-powered chainsaws and other hand and power tools.Travel: This position does not require unique travel. Environmental Conditions/Hazards: The ACE member(s) may encounter environmental conditions/hazards including extreme heat or cold, rocky terrain, swamp or wetland conditions, biting insects, and potentially dangerous wildlife. The member is expected to conduct duties in a safe and orderly manner so as not to endanger self, fellow staff/members or resources. Vehicle and Equipment Use/Safety: If a vehicle is required for the accomplishment of the duties, one will be provided by the NPS or ACE. Any tools required for the accomplishment of the duties will be provided by the site Use of personal protective equipment (PPE), typically provided by the NPS will be mandatory for any activity that requires it. Strict adherence to NPS and ACE equipment training, certification and safety protocols is required. To Apply: Please submit your resume, a cover letter demonstrating your interest and experience, and contact information for three professional/academic references to ACE’s online application page for this position on our website. Early consideration will be given as applications are received. This position may close at any time. If you have any questions regarding this position please feel free to contact ACE EPIC Senior Member Manager, Sabrina Caruso.If you meet at least 70 percent of the qualifications, we want to hear from you!ACE participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information when you are enrolled in a program to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S.EEO: Employment or Service with ACE is based upon ability, qualifications, attitude, and job-related factors. Every qualified employee, member, or applicant has the same opportunity for recruitment, hire, training, transfer, promotion, compensation, demotion, termination, benefits, employee activities, and general treatment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, creed, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, citizenship status, genetic information, veteran or military status, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, medical condition, marital or parental status, political affiliation, ethnicity, hair texture or style, arrest record, caste, hereditary status, endogamy, or any other classification protected by applicable local, state, or federal law.

jobs.title: Fort Monroe Chesapeake Gateways Ambassador at Appalachian Conservation Corps
jobs.description: Employer: Appalachian Conservation Corps Expires: 10/25/2026 Title: Fort Monroe Chesapeake Gateways AmbassadorLocation: Based out of Fort Monroe National Monument (Hampton, VA)Dates of Service: November 30th, 2026 – November 12th, 2027 (50-week term commitment)Pay: $760/week ($600/week stipend + $160/additional benefit)Status: This is a full-time, temporary, AmeriCorps National Service position.Questions? Contact ACCIPrecruiting@conservationlegacy.org Please submit a resume and cover letter via our website, www.appalachiancc.org/individualplacements. Applications will be accepted until October 11th. Appalachian Conservation Corps: Our Individual Placement program works to connect young people to conservation service across Appalachia and neighboring communities in Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, DC, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. ACC is a program of Conservation Legacy, a nationwide network of conservation organizations. When joining this AmeriCorps program, participants commit to a term of service at their placement site and in return gain hands-on experience and a variety of benefits to help them succeed in achieving their career goals. ACC welcomes national applicants but also emphasizes the engagement of local individuals who represent the communities in which they serve. National Park Service Chesapeake Gateways:Chesapeake Bay Gateways is a congressionally authorized partnership park established in 1998 that connects more than 300 parks, refuges, museums, historic sites, trails, water-access points, and communities across the Chesapeake Bay watershed. The National Park Service provides partners with expertise, funding, training, and technical assistance to strengthen visitor experiences and connect people with the Chesapeake’s natural resources, cultural heritage, recreational opportunities, and communities.The Appalachian Conservation Corps and National Park Service are seeking three Chesapeake Gateways Ambassadors to serve at national parks within the watershed. Each Ambassador will work with an on-site NPS supervisor as part of their host park’s interpretive and visitor-services team while also participating in a regional cohort. Together, Ambassadors will share ideas, participate in training, learn from one another, and help strengthen connections among national parks, Network partners, gateway communities, and visitors. Host Park and Local PlacementFort Monroe National Monument (FOMR) is located in Hampton, Virginia, at Old Point Comfort, where the James River meets the Chesapeake Bay. Long before the construction of the present-day Fort Monroe, this landscape and its surrounding waters were important to Indigenous peoples of the Chesapeake region. Its location at the entrance to the James River also made Point Comfort strategically significant to early English colonists, who established Fort Algernourne here in 1609 and later Fort George in the 18th century. Fort Monroe, constructed beginning in 1819, continued the site's centuries-long role in the defense of the Chesapeake Bay and Hampton Roads.Today, Fort Monroe preserves and interprets a nationally significant cultural landscape with stories spanning Indigenous history, early European colonization, the arrival of the first recorded Africans in English North America at Point Comfort in 1619, coastal defense and military history, slavery and freedom, the Civil War-era “Contraband Decision” and its implications for emancipation, and the site's continuing connections to the people, communities, and environment of the Chesapeake Bay.The Ambassador will be integrated into Fort Monroe’s interpretation and visitor services program under the supervision of the Interpretation, Education, and Visitor Services Program Manager. Working alongside NPS staff and partners, the Ambassador will provide visitor services, develop and deliver interpretive programming, and help connect Fort Monroe’s resources and stories to the broader Chesapeake Bay watershed and Chesapeake Gateways Network. The placement will also provide opportunities for interdisciplinary work involving cultural and natural resource stewardship, community engagement, partnerships, special events, and coastal resilience.Fort Monroe is located within the Hampton Roads metropolitan area, with access to the surrounding communities of Hampton, Newport News, Norfolk, and other destinations throughout southeastern Virginia. Because of the location of the park and the transportation needs associated with the position, the Ambassador will need reliable personal transportation.The Ambassador will support the host park through a combination of public contact, program development, research, digital content, special events, community outreach, and other interpretive or visitor-service activities. Housing is not provided. Some overnight/weekend travel may be expected. Park-Specific ResponsibilitiesStaff visitor-contact locations and provide visitor services to orient visitors to Fort Monroe and surrounding Chesapeake resources.Assist with interpretive programs, educational programs, special events, and public programs.Develop and deliver formal and informal interpretation of Fort Monroe’s cultural and natural resources for visitors of different ages, backgrounds, interests, and abilities.Research and develop new interpretive programs, digital content, and visitor-facing materials on Chesapeake-related themes, resources and stories.Promote exploration of related Chesapeake sites throughout the region.Contribute to projects involving: Coastal resilienceMaritime historyNatural resourcesChesapeake landscape and its communitiesStories of people who lived, worked, traveled, and sought freedom at Point ComfortSupport major commemorative events, including African Landing, Juneteenth, and America 250 activities.Take ownership of a substantive project that provides a lasting benefit to Fort Monroe, its visitors, and the broader Chesapeake Gateways Network. Shared ResponsibilitiesResponsibilities will vary by host park but may include:Researching and interpreting connections among the host park, surrounding communities, and the Chesapeake Bay watershed.Creating digital media, trip-planning information, interpretive materials, or other public-facing products to share with the broader cohort.Supporting engagement with young people, schools, community organizations, and audiences that may face barriers to outdoor recreation or heritage experiences.Collaborating with the other Chesapeake Gateways Ambassadors on shared projects, presentations, and professional-development activities.Documenting activities, accomplishments, visitor contacts, lessons learned, and recommendations for future programming.Participating in other National Park Service activities and projects based on the Ambassador’s interests, development goals, and the needs of the host park.Preferred Qualifications:Some college coursework or equivalent education, training, or experience in natural resources, environmental studies, history, public history, education, interpretation, recreation, or a related field.Experience working in public-facing, visitor-service, interpretive, educational, community, or customer-service roles.Strong written and verbal communication skills and an interest in engaging with a variety of audiences.Interest in natural and cultural resources, history, public lands, the Chesapeake Bay watershed, or community-based storytelling.Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team while also completing independent projects and assignments.Willingness to learn, take initiative, and engage with a variety of park programs, partners, visitors, and subject areas.Comfortable working both indoors and outdoors and participating in programs and special events in varying seasonal conditions.Reliable personal transportation for travel to and from the duty station and other local work locations as needed. Minimum Requirements: To qualify, you must be between the ages of 18 and 26 (or 35 if a US Veteran), and a US citizen that has received a high school diploma or GED. All offers of employment are conditional upon completion of an acceptable check of the National Sex Offender Public Registry and federal criminal background check. Must be eligible to receive an AmeriCorps Education Award. In addition, applicants must: Possess a valid driver’s licenseReliable transportation Time Requirements:These positions are full-time, 40 hour/week.Typically, this position is expected to serve Monday to Friday, but exact service schedules may vary. A half hour lunch break will not be counted towards AmeriCorps service.Member may be required to participate in national, state, or local service projects or events as part of their service term.Some overnight/weekend travel for special events. Benefits: $760 week stipend paid bi-weekly ($600 living stipend + $160 additional member benefit)Option to enroll in free health/vision/dental insurance$7,395 AmeriCorps Segal Education Award upon successful completion of 1700 hour minimum service term (award amount varies based on length of commitment and can be used for paying off federal student loans or paying tuition for a Title IV accredited college) $1,750 professional development fund for certifications, trainings, conferences, and travel reimbursementsPublic Land Corps Non-Competitive Hiring Certificate upon successful completion – non-competitive hiring status for two years when applying for federal positions.Possible federal student loan forbearance and interest payoffMember Assistance Program – 3 free sessions of support with a counseling or work-life balance specialist Depending upon the academic institution and program, positions may fulfill internship requirements Professional development opportunities (mentorship, resume support, alumni listserv, etc.) and exposure to natural resource career paths Evaluation and Reporting:As an AmeriCorps member, performance will be evaluated on whether the member has completed the required number of hours, the member has satisfactorily completed assignments, and if the member has met other performance criteria that were clearly communicated at the beginning of the term of service.Reporting requirements include, but are not limited to: bi-weekly timesheets and accomplishment tracking. Our Commitment:Conservation Legacy is committed to the full consideration of all qualified individuals and will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to perform essential job functions. Physical requirements may include periodic overnight travel, non-traditional work hours, ability to move across varied terrain, use program-specific tools and a range of technology on an infrequent or frequent basis. jobs.title: Program Operations Intern - Civic Education at Cato Institute
jobs.description: Employer: Cato Institute Expires: 10/25/2026 To be considered for this role, you must apply directly through our online application. OverviewSphere Education Initiatives is a nonpartisan educator professional development program housed at the Cato Institute that provides teachers and administrators in grades 5–12 with viewpoint-diverse resources to strengthen free speech, civil discourse, and civic culture in their classrooms. Sphere's flagship program is Sphere Summit — a fully funded, five-day in-person event held twice each summer in Washington, DC — alongside Sphere on the Road (school and district visits), the Sphere Alumni Fellowship (a six-month program for Summit graduates), and an expanding library of curriculum resources, including lesson plans, toolkits, and multimedia content. The internship covers program operations, curriculum creation, and administrative duties. The workload is event-focused and logistically demanding during Summit season, shifting to content development and program support at other times. It is ideal for applicants interested in K–12 civics education and educator professional growth who are also dependable, organized, and comfortable with operational tasks — including inventory management, shipping coordination, and CRM maintenance — as well as more in-depth curriculum and program work.ResponsibilitiesAssist with the Sphere Summit application review and program development, including communicating with participants and handling logistical arrangements.Provide operational support for Sphere on the Road and other Sphere events, including preparing materials, shipping packages, and managing inventory using EZO.Maintain and update Sphere's educator contacts and program records in Salesforce, including list maintenance and record management.Develop curriculum resources for teachers of grades 5–12 that promote civil discussion, diverse viewpoints, and civic participation in the classroom.Assist with the Sphere Alumni Fellowship, including organizing events, conducting research, and managing program logistics.Assist in creating program materials, lookbooks, and other communications as assigned.Assist at Sphere Summit and other Cato events as needed, including participant support and on-site logistics.Required QualificationsStrong interest in K–12 civic education, civil discourse, and educator professional development; comfortable engaging respectfully and constructively with educators and participants from diverse viewpoints.Understanding of libertarian and classical-liberal thought and aligning with Cato's principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace, while recognizing that Sphere's programs are explicitly nonpartisan and support educators across the political spectrum.Clear written and verbal communication; professional demeanor in participant-facing and vendor-facing interactions.Reliable follow-through in event-driven settings with changing priorities and strict logistics timelines.Professionalism, humility, and an entrepreneurial mindset — willingness to handle both substantive project work and operational responsibilities as needed.Professionalism, reliability, and attention to detail — this work requires accuracy in both data handling and written output, as well as consistent follow-through across operational and content tasks.Preferred QualificationsFamiliarity with Salesforce or a similar CRM for contact management, list hygiene, and basic reporting.Proficient in Microsoft Excel for list management and basic tracking.Prior experience in program administration, event coordination, or education-related work through a school, nonprofit, or civic organization.Knowledge of K–12 curriculum design or educational content development.The Cato Internship ProgramCato’s paid internships are available for undergraduates, recent graduates, graduate students, law students, and early-career professionals who are strongly committed to individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace—principles that together form libertarianism, also known as “classical liberalism,” “market liberalism,” or, to many of our international friends, simply “liberalism.” All Cato interns participate in the same intensive seminar series, which covers a wide range of topics in history, philosophy, policy, and professional development. Interns also assist with events and occasionally support Cato staff with other daily tasks. Interns receive competitive pay. Part-time roles are adjusted accordingly and require a minimum of 25 hours per week. Program participants must be able to attend in person in Washington, DC.For more information about the internship program and experience, we encourage you to explore our website. jobs.description: Employer: Hackensack Meridian Health Expires: 10/29/2026 OverviewWorking under the direction of a credentialed PI at Hackensack Meridian Health, the Intern, Research handles tasks as assigned by physician mentors. This role will primarily be involved in a research project under a physician mentor with a focus in the area of cancer care. This role provides support as needed and gains on the job experience. The projects are IRB-approved protocols submitted by staff physician mentors.The Center for Discovery and Innovation- CDI was established by Hackensack Meridian Health (HMH) as an academic basic and translational research enterprise to rapidly translate science innovation to the clinic and to improve outcomes for patients with cancer, infectious diseases, autoimmune disease and other acute and chronic diseases. The CDI has grown rapidly since its origins in 2019, and now has 39 labs, 200+ scientists and allied personnel supported by 78 NIH and DoD grants and more than 87 other grants and contracts. Areas of expertise include genomics, epigenetics, drug resistance, stem cell biology, drug discovery, diagnostics and biomarker development, rheumatology and pharmacology.The research intern would be working under the guidance of principal investigator. The research intern would be working on a project analyzing steroid sensitivity in patients. For this project, the research intern would coordinate sample acquisition from the research coordinator. The research intern would be performing the fluorescein labeled dexamethasone binding assay for human samples. This involves monocyte isolation from the human blood samples acquired and performing binding studies with fluorescein labeled dexamethasone. The research intern would also assist with laboratory maintenance and supply ordering for this project. The research intern would also assist with data acquisition and analysis. jobs.title: Spring 2027 Public Programs (Paid) Intern at Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum
jobs.description: Employer: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum Expires: 10/30/2026 Internship: Public Programs (Paid)For application deadlines and internship dates, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get-involved/internships.Museum Overview: Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum has been called the “Smithsonian of country music,” celebrated for its broad cultural impact, educational mission, and unrivaled collection of historically important artifacts. Chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964, the Museum is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, educational organization that documents and interprets the history of country music. The Museum collects objects and archival materials that illustrate the evolving history and traditions of country music and provides diverse learning opportunities through educational programs, publications, and exhibitions. First opened in 1967 on Nashville’s Music Row, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum launched its current downtown location in 2001. In 2014, the Museum unveiled a $100 million expansion that doubled its footprint. The Museum now encompasses 350,000 square feet of exhibition galleries, archival storage, retail stores, and event space. The Museum owns Hatch Show Print, a letterpress print shop opened in 1879, and it operates Historic RCA Studio B, where Dolly Parton, Elvis Presley, and many others recorded. In addition, the Museum offers the Taylor Swift Education Center for students, teachers, and families, and dedicated performance spaces in the CMA Theater and Ford Theater, both of which regularly host nationally recognized live music and cultural events.In 2024, the Museum was awarded the prestigious National Medal of Arts by President Joe Biden. The medal is the highest award given to artists and arts institutions by the United States government. The White House Citation, which accompanied the medal, recognized the Museum’s work, which “preserves history, honors giants of the genre, and inspires future generations to write their own songs about the American story.”Internship Program Overview: The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum offers paid internships to full-time college students (undergraduate and graduate) that advance the educational goals of the intern and help to promote the Museum’s mission. The Museum’s internship program offers work-based learning opportunities that introduce college students to museum-related careers and other professions found in large cultural organizations. Internships are designed for a maximum commitment of 25 hours per week for 12 weeks with consideration given to individual university requirements. Additional adjustments to the 12-week, 25-hour schedule will be at the discretion of the internship supervisor. Educational programs which operate on a quarterly basis may be accommodated. jobs.description: Employer: Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum Expires: 10/30/2026 Internship: Events (Paid)For application deadlines and internship dates, please visit: Countrymusichalloffame.org/support/get-involved/internships.Museum Overview: Accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum has been called the “Smithsonian of country music,” celebrated for its broad cultural impact, educational mission, and unrivaled collection of historically important artifacts. Chartered by the state of Tennessee in 1964, the Museum is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, educational organization that documents and interprets the history of country music. The Museum collects objects and archival materials that illustrate the evolving history and traditions of country music and provides diverse learning opportunities through educational programs, publications, and exhibitions.First opened in 1967 on Nashville’s Music Row, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum launched its current downtown location in 2001. In 2014, the Museum unveiled a $100 million expansion that doubled its footprint. The Museum now encompasses 350,000 square feet of exhibition galleries, archival storage, retail stores, and event space. The Museum owns Hatch Show Print, a letterpress print shop opened in 1879, and it operates Historic RCA Studio B, where Dolly Parton, Elvis Presley, and many others recorded. In addition, the Museum offers the Taylor Swift Education Center for students, teachers, and families, and dedicated performance spaces in the CMA Theater and Ford Theater, both of which regularly host nationally recognized live music and cultural events.In 2024, the Museum was awarded the prestigious National Medal of Arts by President Joe Biden. The medal is the highest award given to artists and arts institutions by the United States government. The White House Citation, which accompanied the medal, recognized the Museum’s work, which “preserves history, honors giants of the genre, and inspires future generations to write their own songs about the American story.”Internship Program Overview: The Country Music Hall of Fame® and Museum offers paid internships to full-time college students (undergraduate and graduate) that advance the educational goals of the intern and help to promote the Museum’s mission. jobs.description: Employer: Camp Skylemar Expires: 10/31/2026 Camp Skylemar seeks Outdoor Recreation Staff for this summer. jobs.title: Cabin Counselor at Camp Bear Creek
jobs.description: Employer: Camp Bear Creek Expires: 11/01/2026 Cabin Counselor – Summer StaffLocation: Camp Bear Creek – Eastern IowaWebsite: https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/Dates: May 23-July 24, 2027Being a Cabin Counselor is exhausting. It’s messy. It’s challenging. And it’s also one of the most rewarding things you can do with your summer.Camp Bear Creek is a Christian summer camp in Eastern Iowa serving kids from kindergarten through 12th grade. We’re looking for passionate, fun, dedicated people who want to spend a summer making a real difference — in the lives of campers and in their own.What We’re Looking For:We want people who:Love working with kidsCan serve as strong, positive role modelsAre ready to lead Are excited to help young people grow in faithDon’t mind unplugging and spending a summer in the woodsWe aren't going to lie, being a camp counselor is incredibly hard work. You’ll be responsible for the daily care and well-being of the campers in your cabin — making sure they eat, sleep, brush their teeth, wear socks, and feel safe. It looks different each week and could mean sitting up with them at night when they're scared of the dark. It means teaching them how to paddle a kayak, supporting them at the rock wall/zip lines, building fires for skillet enchiladas (you’re going to love it), dancing to Grooveship worship and answering their questions about Jesus in Bible It also means picking up a kid when they fall in the dirt, giving them a high five when they finally hit the bullseye in archery, and letting them cover you in mud in the creek. It's all part of walking alongside campers through a week of fun, growth, and faith—and helping give them a summer they'll never forget.At Camp Bear Creek, counselors don’t just supervise- they lead. You’ll gain real world experience in:Leadership and public speakingCurriculum planning and facilitationConflict resolution and creative problem-solving Teamwork across diverse backgrounds. These soft skills are essential in every career field. You’ll also lead a variety of camp activities and work with different age groups- giving you the opportunity to grow into a well-rounded leader. We are also willing to work with you to ensure that this job can be used for internship credit in fields like Education, Public Health, Recreation & Leisure, Youth Services, Psychology and more. However, any student in any field can benefit from a summer camp experience like this. You’ll be part of an incredible team of about 30 college-aged staff from across Iowa, the U.S., and even around the world. We work hard. We play hard. We show up for each other every day. You’ll be surrounded by people who push you to grow — and who feel like family by the end of week one. This is more than a job. It’s a ministry, a leadership opportunity, and a summer you’ll never forget. You’ll give this job everything you’ve got — and it will give even more back.So, if you're looking for a summer full of purpose, adventure, community, and growth, don't let this opportunity pass you by. For more information about working at Camp Bear Creek or to apply, visit https://bearcreek.camp/current-job-openings/summer-camp/

jobs.title: Safety Intern at Interstates
jobs.description: Employer: Interstates Expires: 11/01/2026 Help Build a Safer Future—Starting with Your CareerAt Interstates, safety is more than a checklist—it is how we care for our people, serve our clients, and pursue a better way to work.As a Safety Intern, you’ll gain hands-on experience in construction and manufacturing safety while working alongside experienced Safety Managers, Safety Technicians, supervisors, and craft professionals. You’ll spend most of your time in the field, applying what you’ve learned in the classroom, building your professional network, and helping ensure everyone returns home safely.What You’ll DoSpend approximately 80–90% of your time supporting active construction sites or manufacturing locations.Conduct safety observations, inspections, site audits, and hazard assessments.Review pre-job assessments and equipment inspections.Assist with toolbox talks, foreman meetings, onboarding, and safety training.Identify hazards and reinforce PPE, safe work practices, and site requirements.Support incident and near-miss investigations and participate in root-cause analysis.Maintain accurate safety documentation, including JHAs, permits, inspections, and reports.Collaborate with field teams to strengthen Interstates’ safety culture.Assist with first-aid training and site first-aid activities, as appropriately trained and authorized.Complete a safety-related project or learning objective that adds value to the team.What You’ll LearnThis internship will help you develop practical experience in:Construction and manufacturing safety processesHazard recognition and risk assessmentJob Hazard Analyses and pre-task planningSafety observations and site inspectionsIncident and near-miss documentationRoot-cause analysisSafety training and employee engagementCommunication with field leaders, crews, and clientsWhat We’re Looking ForCurrently pursuing a degree in Occupational Safety, Industrial Safety, or a related field.Interest in construction, manufacturing, electrical, or industrial safety.Basic understanding of safety principles through coursework or previous experience.Strong communication, organization, and attention to detail.Willingness to learn, ask questions, accept feedback, and speak up about safety concerns.Ability to work effectively with employees at all levels.Willingness to work occasional weekends, as project schedules require.OSHA 10 certification preferred; it may be obtained during the internship.Previous construction or manufacturing experience is helpful but not required. We’re looking for students who are curious, dependable, collaborative, and committed to helping others work safely.Travel: Approximately 80–90%; interns are typically assigned to one U.S. location for the summerOpportunities: National Construction and ManufacturingWhy Intern at Interstates?At Interstates, you’ll be treated as a team member—not just an intern. You’ll receive:Mentorship from experienced safety professionalsCareer coaching and professional developmentHands-on experience on real projectsOpportunities in national construction and manufacturingPer diem and travel pay, as applicableCompany discount programTeam celebrations and community outreach opportunitiesPotential opportunities to continue your career with Interstates after graduationA Safety Culture with Proven ResultsInterstates is committed to a Zero Injury culture, where every employee plays a role in creating a safe workplace. Our safety performance has earned recognition including ABC National Safety Excellence Awards, ABC STEP Diamond Awards, CURT Construction Industry Safety Excellence Awards, and NSC Safest Companies with Distinction awards.In 2024, Interstates reported an EMR of 0.54, TRIR of 0.79, and DART of 0.37—results made possible by the daily commitment of our field leaders, craft professionals, safety teams, and support staff.Ready to turn your classroom knowledge into real-world experience and help build safer workplaces across the country? Apply for the Interstates Safety Internship today.

jobs.title: 2027 Business Placement - Corporate Wellness (Spa & Fitness) at Hilton
jobs.description: Employer: Hilton Expires: 11/01/2026 Exceptional Hospitality Starts with YouAs a participant in our 12-month Corporate Placements Programme in our Corporate Wellness Department, you’re not just gaining hands-on experience at our Europe, Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) Headquarters in Watford – you’re spreading the light and warmth of hospitality by contributing to the memorable experiences that make the stay for every guest.Here’s what you can look forward to as a programme participant:Prepare for a career in hospitality: Embark on a 12-month transformative journey, encompassing a structured framework of learning and development opportunities, business support activities, and ownership of your own project-based initiatives.Gain hands-on operational experience: From day one, you’ll be fully integrated into Team Hilton. Connect with professionals across the business and gain insight into Wellness, Spa and Fitness. Take the opportunity to gain insight into at least one other business area, paving the way for valuable future relationships.Work on real-world projects: Apply your skills on the job through business-driven projects to reinforce your learning and gain hands-on experience.Develop your skills through world-class training and support: Access Hilton University’s e-learning modules and business library while building knowledge through business-driven projects.Grow with personalised guidance: Benefit from regular feedback and coaching to ensure your progress is supported at every stage of the programme.Hilton Perks: Including our Go Hilton Team Member Travel Program, which provides you with access to heavily reduced hotel room rates for you, your family & friends. Salary & Benefits: £27,500 gross per annum & private healthcare. Location: At our EMEA Headquarters in Watford, with some flexibility depending on team and business need. You will benefit from a subsidised restaurant, a games area and a free in-house gym. Our Placement OpportunityYou will collaborate with a team of directors with extensive international experiences in spa, fitness, wellness, and hospitality. Together, you'll contribute to shaping and developing the EMEA wellness strategy across Hilton's multi-brand portfolio.You will experience the dynamic world of wellness at a corporate level, with hotel visits, and exciting projects across the EMEA region. You'll gain hands-on experience in wellness development, operations, and strategy. You'll support impactful activities and deliverables that drive Hilton's wellness initiatives and enhance guest experiences.Here's a glimpse of some of the things you will be working on:Creative Contributions: Bring fresh ideas to Hilton's evolving wellness strategy.Organisational Impact: Assist in coordinating wellness activities across EMEA.Project Execution: Lead and monitor projects, presenting findings to the team.Team Presentations: Share updates and insights during weekly meetings and monthly progress reflections.Networking Opportunities: Attend events and connect with professionals across Hilton's EMEA network, from senior executives to hotel spa managers.Social Media Campaigns: Design and run initiatives that promote Hilton's wellness programmes.Collaborative Projects: Partner with other departments to bring wellness concepts into life across Hilton.Hotel Visits: Explore spa and fitness facilities at various hotels to understand operations and guest experiences firsthand.Data and Analysis: Gather and analyse information to evaluate wellness performance, using tools like Excel and PowerPoint.
